Lokesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:35607
 1 Crr-
 In The High Court Of Madhya
 Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh

On The 3rd Of December, 2025
 Criminal Revision No. 1308 of 2024
 Lokesh
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Deepak Tiwari - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Ms.Neelu Khetra -Ga appearing on behalf of Advocate
 General.
 Order
This criminal revision under section 398 r/w section 401 of the Cr.P.C, 1973 is preferred being
aggrieved by the framing of third head of charge under section 376(D) of the Ipc vide order dated
22.02.
2024 in S.T.No.18/2024 by 5th ASJ, Ratlam arising out of Crime No.600/2023 registered at police station Manak Chowk, Ratlam

. 
2. Facts in brief are that Crime No.600/2023 was registered at police station Manak Chowk, Ratlam under sections 376, 376(2)
(n) & 506 of the IPC on06.11.2023 on the report of prosecutrix NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35607 2 CRR-1308-2024 disclosing duration of offence from 18.07.2022 till 03.03.2023 explaining the delay in filing the FIR that she got terrified by the threat of the revision petitioner.
A statement under section 164 of the Cr.P.C, 1973 was recorded by the JMFC, Ratlam on 09.11.2023.
Further formalities of investigation were completed and a final report under sections 376, 376(2)(n) & 506 of the IPC was submitted against the revision petitioner.

3. Trial Court framed the charges under sections 376(1), 376(2)(n), 376D & 506 Part-II of the IPC and the challenge through this revision petition is the framing of charge under the head no.3 of the impugned order i.e 376D of the IPC on the ground that after investigation the police has not submitted the report under section 376D of the IPC.
The objection (Annexure P/10) regarding release on anticipatory bail does not mention that the prosecutrix was subjected to gang rape.
In the objection for regular bail (Annexure- P/15) also, there was no mention that she was subjected to gang rape.

Accordingly, in the absence of any allegations of gang rape in Annexures P/10 & P/15 as well as no mention of gang rape in the final report submitted by the prosecution, trial court was not justified in framing the charge under section 376D of the IPC, hence prayed for discharge.

5. Heard.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35607 3 CRR-1308-2024 6.
Counsel for the State opposed the criminal revision.
7. Counsel for the victim also prayed for dismissal of the criminal revision.

8. Perused the record.
9.

The statement recorded under section 164 of the Cr.P.C, 1973 by JMFC, Ratlam specifically mentions that on 04.11.2023 the revision petitioner met in the vegetable market at 8 p.m and compelled her to come out of the house under the threat of making viral on social media the video of intimate scene of the revision petitioner.
Under the fear when the victim reached at the place where he has pointed out at 11 p.m, then the revision petitioner and his friend committed rape with her.

The reason for not submitting the report under section 376D of the IPC is mentioned in the final report that during the police custody of the revision petitioner he did not reveal any information regarding the involvement of his friend in the incident.
10.
Annexure P/10 & P/15 are not part of the final report and the reason for not submitting the report under section 376D of the IPC is not convincing.
The trial Court has exercised its jurisdiction properly in framing the charge under section 376D of the IPC also in the light of the statement recorded under section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
The other grounds raised by the revision petitioner have NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35607 4 CRR-1308-2024 to be proved and are matter of defence.
Accordingly, this criminal revision does not succeed and is hereby dismissed.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
